correctness.rationale: For every m>=2 and n>=2m+1 the filter is an exact signed circulant whose weights follow from quadratic normal equations. Cyclic first differences identify the quotient variation norm with an l1 map on the zero-sum subspace. Pairing positive and negative mass gives the exact half-of-two-shift norm, attained by binary block data. Equality to kernel l1 mass requires translates of each same-sign support to be disjoint. The positive block and the two negative edge arcs yield allowed displacement intervals [P,2b-1] and [2m+1,infinity), whose sumsets give the exact iff classification. Critical prerequisites P>=m+1 and b in {a+1,a+2} are proved from the weight sign threshold; finite exact-rational tests of all m=2..20 near both endpoints and support-geometry tests of m=21..120 corroborate only. The Riemann sum establishes the asymptotic. No finite enumeration is presented as proof of an infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The kernel and its mass are acknowledged as prior; the DDZ two-column norm identity is also known. The all-radius exact set of cyclic lengths attaining that upper mass, including isolated resonance, forbidden gap and arithmetic zero-weight exceptions, was not present in the inspected closest research. Its result cannot be deduced solely from the previously known kernel mass because different lengths with the same radius attain distinct gains (five-tap six versus seven sites). Historical priority remains qualified by restricted access to the 1983 overshoot paper and possible unindexed literature.

value.rationale: The cycle-length attainment set is a natural exact robustness invariant: for classic polynomial-preserving smoothing, when does the previously known unconstrained kernel norm actually appear in adjacent variation of a finite periodic signal? A complete all-radius classification with an isolated resonance, a strict gap, eventual saturation, and Pell-type zero-weight exceptions answers it. The five-tap 6-to-7-site drop is a nontrivial finite-size stability phenomenon and explicit binary extremizers make it sharp and usable. The result does not rely on novelty of kernel coefficients or a routine recomputation of a known table; the arithmetic sign-translation geometry is the substantive new classification.
